title: Integrative analysis of programmed cell death pathways reveals prognostic biomarkers and immune infiltration signatures in coronary artery disease.
summary: Machine-learning analysis of coronary-artery-disease data identified the PCDscore and five core genes as prognostic biomarkers, alongside immune-infiltration signatures. These are retrospective, computational associations; they do not establish causal gene function or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Machine-learning feature analysis identifies a programmed-cell-death-related prognostic score (PCDscore), five core genes and associated immune-infiltration signatures.
organization: Patient Service Center, the First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, Xi'an, China

evidence.tested: Europe PMC abstract reports the prognostic score, five core genes and immune-infiltration analysis in the study datasets; this is retrospective biomarker analysis.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility and causal roles of the identified genes were not established
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature analysis identifies a programmed-cell-death-related prognostic score (PCDscore), five core genes and associated immune-infiltration signatures.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
